$$

question.:question/problem:
Consider the following system of equations.

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}x-3y &=-3 \\ -x+3y &=3\end{aligned}\right.
$$

Which of the following statements are true?

Select all that apply.
question.:question/worked-solution:
To classify the system, we first need to find its solution. The augmented matrix for this system is

$$
M=\left[\begin{array}{cc|c}1 & -3 & -3 \\ -1 & 3 & 3\end{array}\right].
$$

Using the method of Gaussian elimination, we can reduce this matrix to row echelon form as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =\left[\begin{array}{cc|c}1 & -3 & -3 \\ -1 & 3 & 3\end{array}\right] & {R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+(1){R}_{1} \\ & ∼\left[\begin{array}{cc|c}1 & -3 & -3 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{array}\right]\end{aligned}
$$

The basic variables are the variables whose coefficients are pivots. Here there is one free variable, $y$. Therefore, since there are infinitely many solutions, we conclude that the system is *consistent dependent*.

As a result, select: The system is consistent dependent.

question.:question/problem:
Consider the augmented matrix $M$, with columns in the order $x,y,z$:

$$
M=\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}0 & -1 & -1 & -4 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{array}\right]
$$

question.:question/worked-solution:
Keeping the columns in the order $x,y,z$, the augmented matrix is

$$
M=\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}0 & -1 & -1 & -4 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{array}\right]
$$

Normalize the first pivot with $R_1\leftarrow (-1)R_1$.

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}0 & 1 & 1 & 4 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 & 0\end{array}\right]
$$

The matrix is in row echelon form. There is one pivot. The two zero rows express $0=0$, so they impose no restrictions. The **basic variable** is $y$; the **free variables** are $x,z$. The remaining equation and its rearrangement are

$$
\begin{aligned}y+z &=4 \\ y &=4-z\end{aligned}
$$

Thus all solutions are

$$
\begin{bmatrix}x \\ y \\ z\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}x \\ 4-z \\ z\end{bmatrix},\quad x,z\in\mathbb{R}
$$

Separating the constant part and the contributions of the two free variables gives

$$
\begin{bmatrix}x \\ y \\ z\end{bmatrix}=\begin{bmatrix}0 \\ 4 \\ 0\end{bmatrix}+x\begin{bmatrix}1 \\ 0 \\ 0\end{bmatrix}+z\begin{bmatrix}0 \\ -1 \\ 1\end{bmatrix},\quad x,z\in\mathbb{R}
$$

The two free parameters range independently over all real numbers, so the solution set is a plane.

question.:question/problem:
Find $\det(C)$ for

$$
C=\begin{bmatrix}0 & 3 & 0 \\ 4 & -1 & 1 \\ 3 & -2 & -1\end{bmatrix}.
$$
question.:question/worked-solution:
Expand across the top row with signs $+,-,+$. Delete each entry's row and column to form its minor, then subtract the diagonal products. Terms with a zero top-row entry vanish.

$$
\begin{aligned}M_{12}&=\begin{vmatrix}4 & 1 \\ 3 & -1\end{vmatrix} \\ &=4\cdot (-1)-1\cdot 3 \\ &=-7.\end{aligned}
$$

Combine the signed contributions:

$$
\begin{aligned}\det(C)&=0M_{11}-3M_{12}+0M_{13} \\ &=0-3(-7)+0 \\ &=0+21+0 \\ &=21.\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/problem:
Let $Z=XY.$ What is the value of ${z}_{13}$, if
$X=\begin{bmatrix}-6 & 1 \\ 1 & -6\end{bmatrix}$
$Y=\begin{bmatrix}-2 & 5 & -4 & -2 \\ 4 & -5 & -1 & 5\end{bmatrix}?$
${z}_{13}=$ {{field-1}}
question.:question/worked-solution:
The full matrix product is

$$
Z=\begin{bmatrix}-6 & 1 \\ {\color{lightgray}{1}} & {\color{lightgray}{-6}}\end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix}{\color{lightgray}{-2}} & {\color{lightgray}{5}} & -4 & {\color{lightgray}{-2}} \\ {\color{lightgray}{4}} & {\color{lightgray}{-5}} & -1 & {\color{lightgray}{5}}\end{bmatrix}
$$

Multiplying the $1$st row in $X$ by the $3$rd column in $Y$, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{z}_{13} & =\begin{bmatrix}-6 & 1\end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix}-4 \\ -1\end{bmatrix} \\  & =(-6)(-4)+1(-1) \\  & =24-1 \\  & =23.\end{aligned}
$$

$M=\begin{bmatrix}-5 & 4 \\ 1 & 1\end{bmatrix}$
$N=\begin{bmatrix}4 & -3 & 6 \\ -1 & 4 & 6\end{bmatrix}?$
${l}_{11}=$ {{field-1}}
question.:question/worked-solution:
The full matrix product is

$$
L=\begin{bmatrix}-5 & 4 \\ {\color{lightgray}{1}} & {\color{lightgray}{1}}\end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix}4 & {\color{lightgray}{-3}} & {\color{lightgray}{6}} \\ -1 & {\color{lightgray}{4}} & {\color{lightgray}{6}}\end{bmatrix}
$$

Multiplying the $1$st row in $M$ by the $1$st column in $N$, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{l}_{11} & =\begin{bmatrix}-5 & 4\end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix}4 \\ -1\end{bmatrix} \\  & =(-5)\cdot 4+4\cdot (-1) \\  & =-20-4 \\  & =-24.\end{aligned}
$$
